description: Estimated case capacity in grains of water, to the case mouth. None of these numbers are printed measurements. A cited caseCapacityGrH2O in data/cartridges/cartridges.json, data/cartridges/bots/bullets.json, data/cartridges/bots/loads.json, Hammer's printed Case volume H20 in data/loads/inputs/hammer/case-data.csv, or another printed case-volume file under data/loads removes that cartridge from this table on the next run. Do not copy caseCapacityEstimateGrH2O into a bot cartridge. A bot record's caseCapacityGrH2O, neckLengthIn, and shoulderAngleDeg now fill empty library fields, so an estimate placed there would be shown as published. Load-bot cartridges are included because capacity estimates were handed to the bullet bot. This file does not claim those cartridges.
storageQuestion: The cartridge schema has no estimated-value flag. These numbers were not written into caseCapacityGrH2O. How should an estimate be stored: a caseCapacityEstimateGrH2O field plus a method and source, or an estimated flag on caseCapacityGrH2O?

geometric.summary: Body frustum, shoulder cone, and neck cylinder. Neck inside diameter is the bullet diameter. Neck length is the stored neck, or one bullet diameter when neck length is null (the same assumption as src/lib/geometry.ts). Base outside diameter is the rim diameter plus a fitted rim-class offset (0 for rimless, where the rim is the head). The library has no base, shoulder, or neck outside diameters, so none were copied in. Effective wall, head web, and body taper were fitted on rimless cartridges that have a cited capacity and a shoulder angle, minimizing median absolute error. The fitted wall is thicker than typical brass because the model has no extractor groove. When the parent cartridge is in the calibration set, that parent's residual (model minus cited capacity) is subtracted from the child's geometric estimate.
geometric.preference: When both methods can run, the geometric estimate is kept if its rim-class median absolute error is within 1 gr of the parent-case error. Otherwise the parent-case estimate is kept. The other number is stored as alternate.

parentCase.summary: parent capacity × (child case length / parent case length) + k × (parent bullet diameter² − child bullet diameter²) × child case length. k is fitted on pairs where the parent and the child both have a cited capacity. The adjustment covers a length change and a neck-bore change. It does not add the extra volume of a blown Ackley shoulder; no Ackley cartridge in the calibration set has a cited capacity, and the library has no shoulder diameter. The geometric model does use a stored Ackley shoulder angle when the row has one. A capacity the owner file already labels as an estimate is not used as a parent. When this method, or the geometric method, comes out below the parent's cited capacity for an Ackley Improved cartridge, the estimate is raised to that parent capacity.
parentCase.unit: grains per inch per square inch of bore-area change

printedProfile.method: Reamer diameters are chamber diameters. Subtract body clearance for the case outside, then a tapered body wall (thicker at the web), a neck wall, and a solid head. Clearance and wall were chosen inside typical rifle-case bands to minimize median absolute error on cartridges that have both a printed profile and a published capacity.

inputs.profile: Printed reamer diameters are chamber diameters. Case outside is chamber minus the diametral clearance. Water capacity then removes a tapered body wall, a neck wall, and a solid head web.

assumptions: Printed reamer diameters are chamber sizes. Body clearance 0.006 in and neck clearance 0.004 in on the diameter estimate the case outside. Brass removed: body wall 0.030 in at the web tapering to 0.017 in at the shoulder, neck wall 0.016 in, solid head 0.18 in. Those thicknesses were chosen inside typical rifle-case bands by the median error on published capacities.
Neck length is not stored. Used case length minus the printed length to the neck junction. Chamber diameters were reduced by the fitted clearance, then by the brass wall and solid head.
Superseded by a printed case volume when one is available.
